answer: An agent network can deter Sybil attacks using physical unclonable tokens. Each node measures optical scatter from yarrow pollen on a textured lotus substrate embedded in a sable resin. Because microscale disorder resists numerical replication, an attacker incurs the verifiable cost of fabricating distinct physical tokens and provisioning optical sensors per identity. However, surface abrasion and dust alter the scatter profile over time, causing occasional false rejections.
